newsitem.title: USA: Polyphase sees $100 mln income from stadium.
newsitem.headline: Polyphase sees $100 mln income from stadium.

text.p: Polyphase Corp said on Tuesday it projected a Las Vegas, Nev., stadium it was helping to develop could generate revenues in excess of $1 billion over three years, starting immediately.
If these projections were accurate, Polyphase said it would generate over $100 million in pretax income in fees and equity participation over the three years from the project.

In November, Nevada Stadium Partners, led by Polyphase Chairman Paul Tanner, said it bought land in Nevada. In a long-term deal, Polyphase would be the project manager for a 110,000 seat stadium, convention, entertainment complex there.

The stadium would generate these revenues, part of which would go to Polyphase, from, among other things, presale of luxury box suites, naming rights, concession and merchandising rights and ultimately operations, Polyphase said.

It would be operated by Nevada Stadium Partners, a partnership among Plystadium, Polyphase and Lehman Brothers Holding Inc, the company said. Plystadium was a partnership among Polyphase, Tanner and privately held Hunts Sports and Entertainment, the company said.
Polyphase said it expected the stadium complex to begin operations in mid or late 1999. Preliminary design has been completed and construction was set to start in early 1997, the company said.

Polyphase would oversee all aspects of the venture, including design, construction and development of the stadium, convention center, hotel and retail outlets, it said. It would also manage the sale of all luxury suites, premium seat licenses, marketing and concession rights, and negotiation of all naming rights and merchandise sales.
The company said it retained rights to 14 percent ownership of the project throught conversion of certain subordinated debentures.
